video_goal: Demonstrate the precise visual steps to perform an acid-base titration and identify the endpoint using phenolphthalein.
required_subjects_and_props: Glass burette, burette stand and clamp, Erlenmeyer flask, small funnel, beaker with titrant, phenolphthalein indicator dropper bottle, white ceramic tile

outline_steps.visual_action: A glass burette is clamped vertically to a metal stand, positioned directly above an Erlenmeyer flask resting on a white ceramic tile.
A hand holds a small glass funnel at the top of the burette and slowly pours a clear liquid from a beaker into the burette.
The camera aligns exactly at eye level with the burette's measurement markings, showing the bottom of the liquid meniscus resting perfectly on the 0.0 mL line.
A hand squeezes exactly three drops of clear liquid from a small dropper bottle labeled 'Phenolphthalein' into the clear liquid inside the Erlenmeyer flask.
A hand grips the neck of the Erlenmeyer flask and gently swirls it in a circular motion to mix the liquids.
A hand turns the burette's stopcock valve to a vertical position, allowing a steady, thin stream of clear liquid to fall into the flask below.
One hand continuously swirls the Erlenmeyer flask in circles while the other hand rests firmly on the burette's stopcock.
As the drops hit the liquid in the swirling flask, temporary flashes of bright pink appear and quickly vanish into clear liquid.
The hand on the stopcock turns the valve slightly diagonal, slowing the liquid flow from a steady stream to individual, distinct drops.
A single drop of liquid detaches from the very tip of the glass burette and falls downward.
The single drop hits the liquid in the flask, and as the hand swirls it, the entire volume of liquid turns a permanent, very faint pink color.
The hand immediately twists the stopcock to the fully horizontal position, completely stopping the flow of liquid.
The camera aligns at eye level with the burette again, showing the new position of the meniscus resting on a lower measurement mark.
The faint pink Erlenmeyer flask sits motionless on the white tile directly beneath the closed burette tip.
